newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: FORECAST - Outlook for Boxmore positive - broker.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Outlook for Boxmore positive - broker.

text.p: Northern Ireland-based packaging firm Boxmore International Plc is expected to generate continuing growth into 1997, Davy stockbrokers said in a note.
"In the current year earnings per share (EPS) is forecast to grow by 18 percent while in 1997 our forecast EPS growth rate is 13 percent," Davy analyst Jack Gorman said.

Strong organic growth in the group's PET container sales to the food and drink industries, an additional four month's contribution from folding carton manufacturer GCM, and an increase in group margins were the main drivers of Boxmore's interim results released last week, Gorman said.
Pre-tax profits rose by 39 percent in the first half of 1996 to 7.6 million sterling from 5.5 million sterling on the back of a 34 percent advance in sales to 45.3 million sterling.
Earnings per share grew at a slower rate at 15 percent because of the higher number of shares in issue following the acquisition of healthcare firm GCM in May 1995, Davy said.

"The interim results outturn represents a continuation of the group's impressive growth record of recent years," Gorman said, adding that Boxmore's growth has been generated both internally and through acquisitions.
He said there was scope to fund further capital investment and acquisitions within the group.
"Though on current forecasts the rate of EPS growth will decline compared to recent years, Boxmore has the financial capacity to accelerate its growth profile," Gorman said.
As such Boxmore's potential to invest for accelerated growth can sustain a premium rating to its quoted UK peer group, he added.
